"Okay, well, thank you for having me. So, the Freedom Caucus has always had two primary functions. First, it serves as a check on leadership—especially when leadership strays too far from conservative principles. That’s why we formed back in the '70s. And second, it acts as a platform for members who feel like they’re not being heard within their own party. Now, with the Republican Party out of power in the House, its influence may change—but its core purpose remains intact. The Freedom Caucus isn't just about opposing Democrats; it’s about holding fellow Republicans accountable. Even if we don’t control the majority, we still have the ability to shape policy through coalition-building and strategic positioning. For instance, if the Speaker tries to push legislation that contradicts our values, we can block it or force amendments. And even though we’ve lost the gavel, we still maintain significant leverage because many moderate Republicans depend on our support to pass key bills. So, while our formal power might be reduced, our informal power—and especially our moral authority—is still strong."
